judged_text: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) then group.save, bypassing membership callbacks and making the group.save call dead weight on the happy path. Any denormalized state maintained in GroupUser callbacks or Group save hooks (e.g. user_count recalibration) is skipped, and the trailing group.save implies validation runs on removal when it does not — future maintainers will assume removal is validated and callback-driven when it is neither.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save` (and using `group.save`’s result to decide success vs error). The association deletion is already persisted when `delete` runs, so the subsequent `group.save` does not actually drive the removal and can be misleading (and could even report failure due to unrelated group validations despite the member having been removed). However, the finding’s stronger claim about “bypassing membership callbacks” / “denormalized state maintained in GroupUser callbacks” cannot be verified from this diff because the association type and any callbacks/counter caches are not shown here.
